how do i set how much real money it can use

In Setup → Real money, Schwab, Webull and Claude (for later) → Settings, type the amount in Most real money the bot may use ($); it accepts $10 to $100,000. Choose the broker in Broker for real money, then press Save settings. This only sets a limit; it doesn't switch real money on. A desk trades real money only after its paper results pass the rules, LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED=true is set, and you type the confirmation in the full Setup menu. Each desk also keeps its own $500 budget and never borrows.

what commands does the telegram bot understand

Send your Kestrel bot: /status for how each account is doing and when the autopilot was last seen; /trades for the last 10 finished trades; /report for the latest after-market report (add a date, YYYY-MM-DD, for an earlier one); /pause for no new trades, with stop-losses still working; /resume to let the desks trade again; and /kill SELL EVERYTHING for the emergency stop. Anything else, including /help, gets you the list. It only answers the phone you paired.

why did it buy NIO

NIO is on the day desk's fixed watchlist, so any buy came from the day desk's method. Every buy carries its reason, like the method's name and 'score 1.00 >= 0.9', in the Activity list and the journal, and the after-market report shows what it traded, why, and the team's notes on that decision. If the desk was practicing TJR's model, a score of 1.0 means the full setup happened: hourly trend up, a sweep, a break above the swing high and a pullback into the gap. Check the journal entry for that day for the exact reason.

how do i install kestrel on my mac

It takes about 3 minutes. 1) Click the Download Kestrel for Mac link at the top of the GitHub page and open Kestrel-mac.zip (it unzips itself). 2) Drag Kestrel into your Applications folder; it must live there to update itself. 3) Open it. The first time, macOS blocks it because it isn't from the App Store, so use Open Anyway in System Settings → Privacy & Security. 4) The first time only, a Terminal window installs Python and the bot's libraries, about 2 minutes. 5) The dashboard then appears with the Setup screen on top.

where does the company info on the stock card come from

The name and exchange come from Alpaca when your keys are saved, and the description, sector, industry, website and size from Yahoo Finance. Each stock is looked up once and kept for 30 days, so clicking around never slows the bot down. what happens if the account drops a lot

There are layers. Each position has a stop-loss: 7% on the swing desk, 1-5% sized to the stock on the day desk. If a desk is down more than 3% on the day, it stops buying for that day. If it falls 15% below its best point, the kill switch sells everything that desk owns and halts it, and a real-money desk drops back to paper. Separately, a desk can't go live at all if its paper trading ever dropped more than 10% from its best day.

what's opening_range_breakout

A day-desk method. The first 30 minutes after the open set the day's opening range, and it has no opinion while that range forms. After that, it buys if the price breaks above the range's high and exits if the price falls back below the middle of the range. Like every day trade, anything still open is sold 10 minutes before the close.

is the update out yet? how do i check

In the menu bar choose Kestrel → Check for Updates…, or press Check for updates at the bottom of the Setup screen. If you're current it says "You're up to date". If there's a newer one it shows "Version X is available (you have Y)" with Install and Restart or Later. Your installed version appears at the top right of the Setup screen. Usually you don't need to check: while the app is open it looks for updates by itself when it opens and once a day.

should i pay for alpaca's $99 a month data?

Not for what Kestrel does today. In Kestrel's notes, $99/month is Alpaca's full options feed. The options-gap watcher only needs each contract's daily volume once a day, which Alpaca's free feed has (15 minutes late), and the watcher never trades anyway. For stock prices, the free IEX feed is real-time but covers one exchange (about 2-3% of volume): prices track the market closely, volumes are smaller. The stocks-in-play check compares IEX with IEX, so it stays like for like. All-exchange data needs Alpaca's paid plan.

what's the journal tab for

Journal has two parts. On top is the After-market report, with a date picker for the last week of reports. Below is What the bot did, and why: a time-stamped log of its recent actions and messages, like the daily check-in, trades, pauses, warnings and lessons learned. If something looks off, the journal usually says why. The first report shows up after the first close with the autopilot on.

what does the autopilot do every day

It wakes every 5 minutes on weekdays (New York time). 9:25am: check-in, login warnings, earnings dates, and a re-scan if the stock list is stale. 9:35am: stocks in play. During market hours: the day desk decides every 5 minutes and the swing desk checks its stops. 3:30pm: no new day trades. 3:45pm: the swing decision. 3:50pm: the day desk sells out. 4:10pm: the study. 4:15pm: the options watcher and the weekly TJR test. 4:20pm: the all-stocks scan. 4:25pm: the after-market report.

can kestrel text me when it buys or sells something

Yes. Set up Telegram in Setup step 5 and your private Kestrel bot messages you every buy and sell, with what it spent, what it got back and whether it was a win or a loss, plus the after-close results, the after-market report and anything urgent like a pause or the kill switch. If you'd rather have push notifications, add Pushover in the same step; it sends every buy and sell too. You can use both. The Mac sends them, so it needs to be awake and online.

how far below the buy price are the stops?

Swing desk: a fixed 7% below what it paid, the stop it was tested with. Day desk: half the stock's usual daily range (its 14-day average true range), at least 1% and at most 5%; if the range is unknown, 2%. A wider stop buys a smaller position: no day trade loses more than 0.66% of the desk at its stop, and no position is bigger than 33% of the desk. Honest note: sizing stops to volatility is a common rule of thumb, not a tested edge.

what does paused mean for a strategy

A strategy is paused when it has lost over at least 30 finished trades, with a negative average that's clearly below zero (at least 1 standard error), not just bad luck. While paused it opens no new trades, and the journal says why, but stop-losses and sales still work. Like every lesson, it's re-checked after each finished trade, so it can come off the pause if results change.

what does 'what happens next' in setup mean, and whats start stage 1

Step 3 says in plain English where each desk is (studying, plan ready, paper trading or live) and how many study days are done. When the swing desk can start, a Start Stage 1 paper trading button appears. Stage 1 skips the study month: the swing desk paper trades the momentum method with pretend money, owning the strongest stocks from your watchlist and the daily scan, buying only while the stock and the S&P 500 are above their 200-day averages. It decides 15 minutes before each close, and a tag shows its progress toward 30 trading days.

what's danger news

When news is on, the bot reads recent headlines (the last 3 days) from Alpaca's news feed, or Yahoo without keys. If a stock's headlines contain words like offering, bankrupt, chapter 11, trading halt, delist, going concern, SEC charges, fraud, reverse split, default, restatement or subpoena, it won't buy that stock for now. Stocks in play with danger news are skipped too. News never makes it buy anything; it only keeps it away.

why does the thinking tab say no check yet today

The desk hasn't made a decision yet today. The day desk checks every 5 minutes while the market is open (it starts after 9:30am New York time); the swing desk decides once a day at 3:45pm and only checks its stop-losses before then. If it still says so during market hours, look at the top line: the autopilot may be off or the Mac asleep (Setup step 2).

is paper trading realistic or does it look better than real life?

Close, but not perfect. Alpaca's paper fills are simplified, with no market impact or slippage, so paper looks a bit better than reality; that's one reason real money starts small. The simulation on your Mac fills every order 0.05% worse than the quote to stay honest. Keep the paper amount equal to your real-money cap so paper behaves like your real account. And 30 paper days is a small sample: passing is evidence, not proof.

what has to happen before kestrel can trade my real money?

Four locks all have to be open, and each desk (swing and day) earns it separately. 1) The desk's paper results pass the promotion rules: at least 30 trading days of paper trading, it made money, it beat SPY over the same days, and it never dropped more than 10% from its best day. 2) Your ~/AITrader/.env file says LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED=true. 3) Prices are real-time, meaning Alpaca or Schwab data, not free Yahoo data. 4) You run the promote step and type REAL MONEY exactly. If any one is missing, no real order goes out.

what time does the day desk stop trading

On a normal day the market closes at 4:00pm New York time. The day desk opens no new trades from 3:30pm (30 minutes before the close) and sells everything at 3:50pm (10 minutes before). On early-close days, when the market shuts at 1:00pm, those become 12:30pm and 12:50pm. Stop-losses keep working right up to the sell-off.

how does the swing desk decide what to buy

Right now (Stage 1) it uses momentum. At 3:45pm it lines up every stock it's considering, its watchlist plus up to 30 strong, affordable names from the daily scan, and ranks them by how much they rose over the past 12 months, leaving out the latest month. A stock in the top 20% that's also above its 200-day average is a buy, strongest first, while there are free slots (8 in total) and cash. If SPY itself is under its 200-day average, it holds what it has and buys nothing new.

why is my strategy on half size

Because it's been losing so far. Once a strategy has at least 12 finished trades in that account and its average result is below zero, the bot halves its maximum position size: on the swing desk, 12.5% becomes 6.25% of the desk. It's re-checked after every trade, so once the average turns positive it goes back to normal. If it keeps losing clearly over 30+ trades, it gets paused instead.
